title: SLO Sentinel: graded denylist and backfill recovery
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: transient spikes and noisy tenants were causing sudden SLO violations when our admission controller applied a binary denylist during overload windows. Binary denylists were too blunt: low-volume noisy tenants would be fully blocked while higher-impact noisy tenants kept consuming capacity, producing uneven service degradation and noisy SLO signals. This PR introduces an SLO Sentinel subsystem that implements a graded denylist (per-tenant penalty scores with configurable enforcement tiers) and a complementary backfill recovery mechanism to ensure capacity reclaimed by eviction is used to reduce overall SLO drift rather than causing sharp latency drops elsewhere.

What this change does (summary):
- Introduces graded denylist logic in the admission controller: tenants are assigned a penalty score computed from recent error/latency SLO signals and request surge profile. Enforcement is tiered: soft-warn, rate-cap, partial-deny (probabilistic drop), and hard-deny.
- Adds a backfill recovery agent in the scheduler that tracks reclaimed capacity from denied requests, and backfills queued requests from low-penalty tenants before escalating to hard-deny for others. Backfill is throttled to respect node-level latency budgets.
- Metric and tracing additions for observability: new counters and histograms (redwood.slo.sentinel.penalty_score, redwood.slo.sentinel.enforcement_level_total, redwood.slo.sentinel.backfill_success_total, redwood.slo.sentinel.backfill_latency_ms) and a SLO tag (slo_loss_reason) on request spans to surface denylist-driven degradation.
- Control-plane config: introduces a SLO Sentinel policy CRD (for Private deployments) and new config flags in the hosted control plane for tuning tier thresholds and backfill aggressiveness.
- Safety and rollout: default policy starts in soft-warn mode (no drops) for 72 hours, then automatically enables rate-cap in permissive mode; can be toggled per-customer.
- Tests: unit tests for penalty score computation, integration test (simulated multi-tenant overload) verifying graceful degradation, and e2e smoke for backfill under partial-deny.

Files and areas changed (high level):
- runtime/admission/sentinel.go (new): graded denylist core and enforcement API;
- runtime/admission/policies.go (update): hooks to read penalty and enforce tiers;
- scheduler/backfill_agent.go (new): capacity bookkeeping and backfill algorithms;
- controlplane/policies/sentinel_policy.yaml (new): CRD and default policy;
- telemetry/metrics_registry.go (update): register new metrics and sampling logic;
- docs/observability/slo-sentinel.md (new): runbook and metric meanings;
- tests/unit/sentinel_test.go (new), tests/integration/sentinel_overload_sim.go (new), tests/e2e/backfill_smoke.yaml (new).

- feat(admission): add graded penalty computation and tiered enforcement (Maya Chen)
- feat(scheduler): implement backfill recovery agent and throttle policy (Maya Chen)
- chore(controlplane): add sentinel policy CRD and default permissive policy (Maya Chen)
- feat(telemetry): register sentinel metrics and annotate spans with slo_loss_reason (Maya Chen)
- test: add unit/integration/e2e tests for sentinel and backfill (Maya Chen)
- fix(lint): address golangci lint errors found by CI (Maya Chen)
- docs: add SLO Sentinel observability and tuning guide (Maya Chen)

Review conversation (high level):
- Arjun requested reducing global lock contention in penalty computation and suggested switching to atomic windows rather than a single mutex around the tenant record.
- Author reply: replaced global lock with tenant-local sharded counters and used atomics for hot-path score updates; updated tests for concurrency.
- Lena flagged metric cardinality risk for per-tenant histograms; requested aggregation knobs.
- Author reply: removed per-tenant histograms from the hot path and added aggregated percentiles plus an opt-in per-tenant debug histogram behind config.
- Samir asked for a safety rollback switch and a staged rollout plan for hosted customers.
- Author reply: added a feature-flag gate and a 72-hour soft-warn default policy plus an emergency disable endpoint for operators.
- CI initially: lint failed (golangci had a nil-check warning) and one flaky integration test failed on first run. After fixes: CI passed all checks.

Why this is safe to merge:
- Backfill logic only activates once the enforcement tier is at or above rate-cap unless explicitly enabled in config; default behavior is soft-warn (no request drops).
- New metrics and runbook included so SREs can monitor impact in the first 72 hours.
- Includes unit/integ/e2e tests and a rollback feature flag.

Migration and operational notes:
- Private customers can install the new CRD via controlplane upgrade; sample sentinel_policy.yaml provided.
- SDKs unaffected; API surface unchanged.
- Observability: dashboards in the Console will be extended in a follow-up PR to plot penalty distribution and backfill effectiveness.

Follow-ups (planned):
- Console dashboarding and alert thresholds for sentinel metrics (ENG-4902).
- Adaptive penalty tuning using model-based anomaly scores (research spike ENG-4977).
- Per-tenant debug view and timeline in Console for customers on Dedicated plans.

Related work: references many prior soft-shed and graceful-fallback efforts (ENG-27109, ENG-314271, SUP-3912), but this PR focuses on per-tenant graded enforcement and actively using reclaimed capacity for backfill instead of leaving it idle.

Merge outcome: squash and merge after approvals; post-merge deploy gated by feature flag rollout and a 72-hour soft-warn observation window.
